clue.text: Lie down in the grass

definitions.meaning: an old verb for lying down or crouching, as an animal in its lair
a creeping weed grass, also called twitch

explanation.surface: An invitation to stretch out on the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Couch as a verb means to recline, and couch grass is a common invasive weed of lawns and gardens.

clue.text: Mistress taking care of nature's mistake

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

indicators.note: a mistake mangles things, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: read as nature is, giving the letters of NATURE plus S

explanation.surface: A kept woman is caring for an error of nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' joins the pieces; CO and NATURES together are rearranged by 'mistake'.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan was a high-class kept lover of a wealthy man, so a mistress in the old sense.

clue.text: One in France expected to be excessive

parts.note: un is French for one
due means expected, as a train due at noon

explanation.surface: A Frenchman supposedly going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means more than is warranted, i.e. going beyond what is appropriate.

clue.text: Shelter in the middle of the shady retreat

indicators.note: the central letter of the word the is taken

parts.note: an arbour is a leafy, shaded bower in a garden

explanation.surface: Taking cover in the centre of a shady garden nook.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour is a refuge for ships, and to harbour is to give refuge.

clue.text: After the game, club splinters

indicators.note: the club comes after the game in the answer's order

parts.note: a match is a sporting game
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: After the match, someone's club is smashed to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a wood is a club with a large head, originally made of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchwood is wood broken into tiny fragments, a mass of splinters.

clue.text: Lamented departed antipodean bird-man

parts.note: the moa was a giant flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct
Ned is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: Someone mourned the passing of a half-bird, half-man from Down Under.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament is to grieve aloud, which is what someone who moaned did.

clue.text: Old customs officer is met and knocked out

indicators.note: something knocked out of shape is rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A former excise man is encountered and floored.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidesman was a historical customs official who boarded ships arriving on the tide.

clue.text: It's buried peacefully and exotically under door

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: a hatch is a small door or opening
et is French, so foreign, for and

explanation.surface: Something laid to rest calmly and in foreign style beneath an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'bury the hatchet', meaning to make peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury the hatchet is to end a quarrel, so this axe is the thing interred in peacemaking.

clue.text: Obvious strain grand slam bidding precludes

parts.note: overt means open and obvious
to rick is to sprain or strain a joint

explanation.surface: A clear injury that a sweeping victory rules out.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a grand slam contracts for all thirteen tricks, so no extra trick beyond the contract is possible.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge an overtrick is a trick won beyond the contract; bidding all thirteen leaves none spare.

clue.text: Dutch leader taken in by superior Venetian trick

indicators.note: one piece is enclosed within the other

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice

indicators.note: the first letter of Dutch is used

explanation.surface: A Dutch chief is duped by a Venetian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a crafty trick or ruse.

clue.text: Secret sort of delivery

definitions.meaning: an ... delivery is a ball bowled or thrown with the hand below the shoulder

explanation.surface: A covert way of bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand describes sly, covert dealing and also a below-shoulder throwing or bowling action.

clue.text: What to do with a measure? Use feet

definitions.text: What to do with a measure?
definitions.meaning: to ... a measure is an old phrase for dancing

explanation.surface: Advice on dancing: get your feet moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading a measure means dancing, and treading is stepping with the feet.

clue.text: What better hopes can be had from this Government?

indicators.note: to be had is to be fooled, so these letters are tricked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cynical question about whether the ruling party can offer anything better.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase denotes those in authority, the ruling establishment.

clue.text: Planet — it has to spin

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a turn is a spin or rotation

explanation.surface: A remark that planets must rotate.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the ringed sixth planet from the Sun.

clue.text: Four identical notes conceal a secret

indicators.note: the outer letters hide the other piece inside them

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, here four times

explanation.surface: A musical phrase repeating one note hides something.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private conversation between two, so confidential.

clue.text: Retired hand involved in cut, with hours reduced

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped up inside the other

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A worker who has stopped is caught up in cuts to working hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Part-time work is employment for fewer hours than full-time.

clue.text: Put on the outside, ran first in classic, showing staying power

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: to endue is an old verb for putting on clothing
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening letter of classic is taken

explanation.surface: A racehorse wore something extra and led in a classic race, proving its stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: A classic is one of the five major British flat horse races, such as the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is stamina, the capacity to keep going.

clue.text: Are not held by friend of an older generation?

indicators.note: one piece is contained within the other

parts.note: a pal is a friend
contracted to aren't, giving those letters

explanation.surface: Someone denies being clutched by an older friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Parental means relating to mothers and fathers, the generation above.

clue.text: Nobody play-acting a Liberal ideal

parts.note: not I suggests no one at all
on means performing on stage

explanation.surface: No one acting a Liberal part is the perfect fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional means existing only as an idea, hypothetical.

clue.text: Stroke, perhaps, for a bumper at Cambridge

definitions.meaning: stroke is the rower nearest the stern who sets the pace
in Cambridge bumps races, rowing crews try to bump the boat ahead

explanation.surface: A rower in a Cambridge boat race.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke is one kind of rower, and bumps races at Cambridge are contested by rowers.

clue.text: Sabotaged weapon — one held by leaders of Social Democrats

indicators.note: one piece is enclosed by the others
the initial letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: a pike is a long spear

explanation.surface: Political saboteurs hold a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To spike something is to thwart it, as in spiking a plan.

clue.text: Digger — mole comprises one

indicators.note: the outer piece takes in the other

parts.note: a mole is a stone pier or breakwater
taken as written

explanation.surface: An excavator: the burrowing animal counts as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer was a soldier who dug trenches and cleared ground ahead of an army.

clue.text: Miserly eccentric?

definitions.meaning: a screw is slang for a miser

explanation.surface: Is a tight-fisted person odd?
explanation.definitionFit: Screwy is slang both for stingy and for crazy or odd.

clue.text: Plain glass used in 20's wagon

parts.note: a prairie is a grassy plain
a schooner is a tall drinking glass

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel found in a settler's vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie schooner was a covered wagon used by North American settlers heading west.

clue.text: Lawmen have no ship

indicators.note: no means without, so the letters are taken away

parts.note: to have is to possess
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: The law enforcers lack a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law.

clue.text: Not a top dressing in the nursery

definitions.text: Not a top dressing in the nursery

parts.words: Not a top dressing in the nursery
parts.note: a garden-sounding dressing that in fact covers a baby's bottom

explanation.surface: Something that is not spread over a plant nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's absorbent undergarment is a dressing for the bottom, not the top.

clue.text: Cook one of the sources of 11

explanation.surface: Cooking with one of the forces in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is a method of cooking, and steam drove engines as a source of power.

clue.text: Disguise put on here immediately after that

indicators.note: to disguise is to alter appearance, so these letters change order

explanation.surface: A costume worn here.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereupon means at once following that event.

clue.text: Doctor learnt in city, unceasingly

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician trained in a cathedral city without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means forever, without end.

clue.text: Used by poets as alternative to reason?

definitions.text: Used by poets as alternative to reason?

parts.words: Used by poets as alternative to reason?
parts.note: a nod to the phrase without ... or reason, and a device of verse

explanation.surface: A poetic substitute for logic.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching line-end sounds are a poetic device, and the idiom pairs it with reason.
